I've been growing stevia here for years now. It sells to the extract factory and the price has been okay, better than wheat or corn on this small 3 mu plot. Let me think through what I'll do this year.

I'll buy improved seedlings from the same dealer in town — the ones from Jiangxi company did well last year, about 250 kg dry leaf per mu after two cuttings. No point saving seed myself, stevia is hard to grow from seed, everyone transplants.

For fertilizer, stevia wants a lot of leaf growth so nitrogen matters. Last year I put about 2 bags of compound fertilizer (45%, 15-15-15) as base before transplanting, that's about 50 kg, giving roughly 7-8 kg of each N, P, K per mu. Then I topdress urea twice — once after the plants settle in May, once after first cutting in July. Maybe 15 kg urea each time per mu, that's another 14 kg N. So total about 20 kg N, 8 kg P, 10 kg K per mu. I'll add a little potash before the second growth flush because my neighbor Old Wang said it helped his leaf quality. Maybe 5 kg extra potassium chloride.

Water — I have the well so I irrigate when it gets dry. After transplanting I water right away, then again a week later to make sure they take. Then during summer if no rain, maybe every 10-15 days. Probably 5 times total across the season.

Pests — aphids and leaf miners always come. I spray when I see them, usually 3 times: once in June, once after first cut when new leaves flush, once more if needed in August. I don't want damaged leaves because the factory docks the price.

Tillage — I rotary till before transplanting, that's enough for stevia, roots aren't deep.
